rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says God accepted repentance from the Prophet, the Emigrants, the Helpers, and the three men.
rows.anchor: {الثلاثة الذين خلفوا} [التوبة: 118] هلال بن أمية، وكعب بن مالك، ومرارة بن ربيعة

rows.speaker: أبو مالك
rows.claim: Abu Malik identifies the three left behind as Hilal ibn Umayya, Kaʿb ibn Malik, and Murara ibn Rabiʿa.
rows.anchor: عن أبي مالك، قال: " {الثلاثة الذين خلفوا} [التوبة: 118] هلال بن أمية، وكعب بن مالك، ومرارة بن ربيعة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima likewise names Hilal ibn Umayya, Murara, and Kaʿb as the three men.
rows.anchor: {وعلى الثلاثة الذين خلفوا} [التوبة: 118] قال: هلال بن أمية، ومرارة، وكعب بن مالك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb recalls being unusually well supplied for the campaign but delaying preparation until the army had departed, after which the Prophet ordered people not to speak to them.
rows.anchor: لما خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قلت: أتجهز غدا ثم ألحقه فأخذت في جهازي، فأمسيت ولم أفرغ

rows.speaker: ابن شهاب
rows.claim: Ibn Shihab recounts Tabuk, the three named men and roughly eighty others staying behind; the three admitted fault truthfully, while others swore excuses and were accepted outwardly.
rows.anchor: والثلاثة الذين خلفوا: رهط منهم: كعب بن مالك، وهو أحد بني سلمة، ومرارة بن ربيعة، وهو أحد بني عمرو بن عوف، وهلال بن أمية

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb says he missed no expedition except Tabuk and Badr; no one was blamed for missing Badr because the Muslims had unexpectedly met their enemy while seeking a Quraysh caravan.
rows.anchor: لم أتخلف عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة غزاها قط إلا في غزوة تبوك، غير أني قد تخلفت في غزوة بدر

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb prized his pledge at al-ʿAqaba above even the better-known battle of Badr.
rows.anchor: شهدت مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة العقبة حين تواثقنا على الإسلام، وما أحب أن لي بها مشهد بدر

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb says the Prophet clarified the campaign's destination so Muslims could prepare; Kaʿb nevertheless delayed despite being unusually well supplied.
rows.anchor: فجلى للمسلمين أمرهم ليتأهبوا أهبة غزوهم

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb repeatedly failed to finish preparing, then regretted not catching up; after the army left, he saw no comparable stay-behind except a suspected hypocrite or an excused weak person.
rows.anchor: وطفقت أغدو لكي أتجهز معهم، فلم أقض من جهازي شيئا، ثم غدوت فرجعت ولم أقض شيئا

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: At Tabuk the Prophet asked about Kaʿb; a man blamed his fine clothes, and the Prophet later recognized Abu Khaythama approaching through the mirage.
rows.anchor: فقال رجل من بني سلمة: يا رسول الله حبسه برداه والنظر في عطفيه

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: When the Prophet was returning, Kaʿb considered inventing an excuse but resolved that no lie would save him and chose to tell the truth.
rows.anchor: فلما قيل: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قد أظل قادما زاح عني الباطل

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: More than eighty stay-behinds offered excuses and oaths; the Prophet accepted their outward claims and left their inner states to God, but told Kaʿb that his truthful admission meant he must await God's judgment.
rows.anchor: فطفقوا يعتذرون إليه ويحلفون له، وكانوا بضعة وثمانين رجلا، فقبل منهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم علانيتهم

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb admitted having no excuse and hoped for God's forgiveness; the Prophet affirmed that he had told the truth and ordered him to wait for God's decision.
rows.anchor: والله ما كان في عذر، والله ما كنت قط أقوى ولا أيسر مني حين تخلفت عنك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Men of Banu Salima urged Kaʿb to use the excuses others gave, and he nearly retracted, but learned that two others had made the same truthful admission.
rows.anchor: فاتبعوني وقالوا: والله ما علمناك أذنبت ذنبا قبل هذا، لقد عجزت أن لا تكون اعتذرت إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb asks who else told the truth and is told two men made the same admission; Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ is first named.
rows.anchor: قالوا: مرارة بن الربيع العامري

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Unlike the other absentees, the three were barred from conversation for fifty nights; people shunned them, while Kaʿb's two companions stayed home weeping and Kaʿb kept attending prayer and markets without being answered.
rows.anchor: ونهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المسلمين عن كلامنا أيها الثلاثة من بين من تخلف عنه

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb's cousin Abu Qatada would not answer whether Kaʿb loved God and His Messenger, finally saying that God and His Messenger knew best.
rows.anchor: يا أبا قتادة أنشدك بالله هل تعلم أني أحب الله ورسوله؟ فسكت

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: A man from Ghassan sent Kaʿb a letter inviting him to join the king because the Prophet had shunned him; Kaʿb treated the offer as another trial and burned it.
rows.anchor: فإذا فيه: أما بعد فإنه قد بلغنا أن صاحبك قد جفاك، ولم يجعلك الله بدار هوان ولا مضيعة، فالحق بنا نواسك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: After forty nights the Prophet ordered the three to separate from their wives; Hilal's wife was allowed to serve him without intimacy, and Kaʿb sent his wife to her family.
rows.anchor: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يأمرك أن تعتزل امرأتك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb refused to ask permission for his wife to remain with him and completed fifty nights under the ban; at dawn he heard a caller announce good news.
rows.anchor: فلبثت بعد ذلك عشر ليال، فكمل لنا خمسون ليلة من حين نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن كلامنا

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: On the fiftieth morning Kaʿb learned that God had accepted their repentance; people brought him the news, and the Prophet greeted him joyfully as having reached his best day.
rows.anchor: أبشر بخير يوم مر عليك منذ ولدتك أمك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb offered to give all his property in charity, but the Prophet advised him to keep some; he retained his share at Khaybar.
rows.anchor: يا رسول الله إن من توبتي أن أنخلع من مالي صدقة إلى الله وإلى رسوله

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb vowed to speak only truth; he called honesty his greatest blessing and contrasted the truthful trio with the hypocrites condemned in the passage about false oaths.
rows.anchor: والله ما أنعم الله علي من نعمة قط بعد أن هداني للإسلام أعظم في نفسي من صدقي رسول الله

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Kaʿb explains that the three were left in suspense by the Prophet's deferral of their judgment, unlike others whose sworn excuses were accepted; the phrase is not about simply missing the campaign.
rows.anchor: وليس الذي ذكر الله مما خلفنا عن الغزو إنما هو تخليفه إيانا وإرجاؤه أمرنا

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: A further transmission through Kaʿb's son repeats his account of the Tabuk absence; another report from Kaʿb notes that he missed only Tabuk and Badr, for which no one was reproached.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه، قال: لم أتخلف عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزاة غزاها إلا بدرا، ولم يعاتب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أحدا تخلف عن بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly life and its wealth and adornment, dulled by loss and death, resemble rain that produces mixed vegetation for people and animals.
rows.anchor: إنما مثل ما تباهون في الدنيا وتفاخرون به من زينتها وأموالها مع ما قد وكل بذلك من التكدير والتنغيص وزواله بالفناء والموت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the rain grows every kind of plant: grain, legumes, and fruit for people, and grasses and pasture for livestock.
rows.anchor: كالحنطة والشعير وسائر حبوب الأرض والبقول والثمار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's taking its adornment means its beauty appears; its owners think they control what it has grown, but God's decree destroys it by night or day and leaves it cut down.
rows.anchor: يعني: ظهر حسنها وبهاؤها. {وازينت}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crops seem to have never existed; the root of تغن means to dwell or remain, as al-Nābigha's verse illustrates, just as worldly splendor vanishes.
rows.anchor: وأصله: من غني فلان بمكان كذا، يغنى به: إذا أقام به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explains signs for reflective people because they distinguish matters and investigate the realities behind doubts.
rows.anchor: وخص به أهل الفكر، لأنهم أهل التمييز بين الأمور والفحص عن حقائق ما يعرض من الشبه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada warns that people who cling to worldly life will soon be cast off and undone by it.
rows.anchor: لئن تشبث بالدنيا وحدب عليها لتوشكن الدنيا أن تلفظه وتقضي منه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses وازينت as the earth having sprouted and become beautiful.
rows.anchor: {وازينت} [يونس: 24] قال: أنبتت وحسنت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Ubayy ibn Kaʿb taught an added reading that the earth would not be destroyed except for its people's sins; the phrase is absent from the codex.
rows.anchor: فقال عباس بن عبد الله بن العباس: هكذا يقرؤها ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abu Salama reports Ubayy's reading with the added explanation that God destroyed the land only because of its people's sins.
rows.anchor: {كأن لم تغن بالأمس} [يونس: 24] وما أهلكناها إلا بذنوب أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce وازينت as تزينت, assimilating tā into zā and adding a connecting alif; some read وأزينت, but al-Ṭabarī prefers the majority reading by reader consensus.
rows.anchor: والصواب من القراءة في ذلك: {وازينت} [يونس: 24] لإجماع الحجة من القراء عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the gathering for judgment, the disbelievers will seem to have lived only an hour and briefly recognize one another before that recognition ends.
rows.anchor: يتعارفون فيما بينهم، ثم انقطعت المعرفة وانقضت تلك الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those denying God's meeting lose their share of good, denying both divine reward and punishment and bringing ruin upon themselves.
rows.anchor: قد غبن الذين جحدوا ثواب الله وعقابه وحظوظهم من الخير وهلكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their lack of guidance means they were not directed to sound judgment in denying God's meeting, which earned them a punishment they cannot withstand.
rows.anchor: وما كانوا موفقين لإصابة الرشد مما فعلوا من تكذيبهم بلقاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to answer those demanding the promised punishment: he controls neither harm nor benefit for himself in worldly or religious matters except by God's will, and is even less able to know the unseen or Hour without permission.
rows.anchor: لا أقدر لها على ضر ولا نفع في دنيا ولا دين إلا ما شاء الله أن أملكه فأجلبه إليها بإذنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every community has a fixed term for its life; when it arrives, none can delay or advance it because God decreed its time.
rows.anchor: لكل قوم ميقات لانقضاء مدتهم وأجلهم، فإذا جاء وقت انقضاء أجلهم وفناء أعمارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rebukes Pharaoh for professing submission only as punishment and death arrive, after earlier disobedience and corruption by turning people from God's path; Pharaoh should have repented while time remained.
rows.anchor: الآن تقر لله بالعبودية، وتستسلم له بالذلة، وتخلص له الألوهة، وقد عصيته قبل نزول نقمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are told to await the fate of earlier nations: when punishment comes, God destroys the deniers and saves Muhammad and those who believe and follow him, as He saved earlier messengers and their believers.
rows.anchor: ثم ننجي هنالك رسولنا محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم، ومن آمن به وصدقه، واتبعه على دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's saving believers is a sure promise incumbent upon Him, as He did with earlier messengers.
rows.anchor: كذلك نفعل بك يا محمد وبالمؤمنين، فننجيك وننجي المؤمنين بك حقا علينا غير شك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who do good deeds seeking worldly life and its adornment receive their full reward in this life without being shortchanged.
rows.anchor: لا ينقصون أجرها، ولكنهم يوفونه فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says such people receive worldly benefits for good deeds done only for worldly ends, such as prayer or night worship, while their work for the afterlife is lost.
rows.anchor: من عمل صالحا التماس الدنيا صوما أو صلاة أو تهجدا بالليل لا يعمله إلا لالتماس الدنيا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the worldly reward for good performed is paid in this world, while the next verse says such people have only the Fire and their work is void.
rows.anchor: ثواب ما عملوا في الدنيا من خير أعطوه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says that prayer or charity done without seeking God's face is paid back in this world in proportion to what was spent, with no afterlife reward.
rows.anchor: من عمل عملا مما أمر الله به من صلاة أو صدقة لا يريد بها وجه الله أعطاه الله في الدنيا ثواب ذلك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says people whose deeds are not accepted are given their recompense or have it hastened to them in this world.
rows.anchor: ممن لا يقبل منه جوزي به، يعطى ثوابه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says someone whose sole aim and intention is worldly life receives payment for good deeds here, leaving no good deed for which to be rewarded in the afterlife; believers receive reward in both.
rows.anchor: من كانت الدنيا همه وسدمه وطلبته ونيته، جازاه الله بحسناته في الدنيا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains لا يبخسون to mean they are not wronged in the afterlife; in another wording, God gives worldly wealth and livelihood as full recompense to the one seeking only this world.
rows.anchor: وأما المؤمن فيجازى بحسناته في الدنيا ويثاب عليها في الآخرة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says the reward of one who does good for a benefactor rests with God in both the immediate world and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن كعب القرظي، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says nonbelievers may receive worldly recompense for righteous acts such as kinship, charity, and relieving distress, but have no share in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: من عمل عملا صالحا في غير تقوى يعني من أهل الشرك أعطي على ذلك أجرا في الدنيا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: The worldly reward can include expanded livelihood, contentment with possessions, and protection from worldly hardships.
rows.anchor: ويوسع عليه في المعيشة والرزق، ويقر عينه فيما خوله، ويدفع عنه من مكاره الدنيا

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas says this verse concerns Jews and Christians.
rows.anchor: قال: هي في اليهود، والنصارى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan glosses their recompense as their worldly good things or pleasures.
rows.anchor: نوف إليهم أعمالهم فيها قال: طيباتهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, as conveyed by Wahb, identifies the people seeking worldly reward as people of ostentation.
rows.anchor: هم أهل الرياء، هم أهل الرياء

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that on Judgment Day God will expose a Qur'an reciter, a wealthy giver, and a martyr who acted to be called learned, generous, or brave; despite those reputations, they will be first to fuel Hell.
rows.anchor: أول من يدعى به رجل جمع القرآن، ورجل قتل في سبيل الله، ورجل كثير المال

rows.speaker: معاوية
rows.claim: After hearing Abu Hurayra's report, Muʿawiya wept and affirmed its truth by reciting this verse through the statement that their deeds are void.
rows.anchor: صدق الله ورسوله {من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها نوف إليهم أعمالهم فيها} [هود: 15]

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says deeds such as fasting and prayer are not accepted when performed for worldly gain; such people receive their reward here and turn away from the afterlife, yet are not shortchanged in that reward.
rows.anchor: ممن لا يتقبل منه، يصوم ويصلي يريد به الدنيا، ويدفع عنه وهم الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those paid for worldly deeds have only the Fire in the afterlife; their work vanishes because they acted for other than God, so He nullifies its reward.
rows.anchor: لأنهم كانوا يعملون لغير الله، فأبطله الله وأحبط عامله أجره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas, Noah loaded the animals onto the ark, beginning with the durra and ending with the donkey; Satan allegedly entered after Noah said a careless phrase inviting him aboard.
rows.anchor: كان أول ما حمل نوح في الفلك من الدواب الدرة، وآخر ما حمل الحمار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The report says the flood began as springs burst and heaven opened; after forty days and nights the ark rose on mountain-like waves, with iron nails in its planks.
rows.anchor: فكان بين أن أرسل الله الماء وبين أن احتمل الماء الفلك أربعون يوما وأربعون ليلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Noah's son was secretly an unbeliever and assumed a mountain would shield him as mountains usually protected people from rain, but Noah said only those receiving God's mercy could escape.
rows.anchor: وكان شقيا قد أضمر كفرا، {قال سآوي إلى جبل يعصمني من الماء} [هود: 43]

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ascribed to the People of the Book, the water rose fifteen cubits above the mountains and destroyed all living things except Noah and those aboard, as well as the figure ʿUj ibn ʿUnuq in their account.
rows.anchor: وكثر الماء حتى طغى وارتفع فوق الجبال كما تزعم أهل التوراة بخمسة عشر ذراعا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The account dates the period from the flood's onset until the waters receded as six months and ten nights.
rows.anchor: فكان بين أن أرسل الله الطوفان، وبين أن غاض الماء ستة أشهر وعشر ليال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son says he will go to a mountain for shelter; يعصمني means protects or prevents, like the waterskin tie that keeps water from escaping.
rows.anchor: ويعني بقوله: {يعصمني} [هود: 43] يمنعني، مثل عصام القربة الذي يشد به رأسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī parses من as nominative: no one protects from God's decree except the one God shows mercy and saves, namely God; the sense is like saying no deliverer exists except God.
rows.anchor: ف «من» في موضع رفع، لأن معنى الكلام: لا عاصم يعصم اليوم من أمر الله إلا الله

rows.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
rows.claim: Some Kufan grammarians parse من as accusative, the protected object, comparing it with the exception in 4:157; al-Ṭabarī rejects the reading because it requires عاصم to mean معصوم.
rows.anchor: فقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: هو في موضع نصب، لأن المعصوم بخلاف العاصم

rows.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufan argument allows a passive sense in active-form participles, citing دافق, راضية, and the poet's الطاعم الكاسي for meaning poured, pleasing, and clothed.
rows.anchor: معناه والله أعلم مدفوق؟ وقوله: {في عيشة راضية} [الحاقة: 21] معناها: مرضية؟

rows.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
rows.claim: Some Basran grammarians read إلا as لكن, or understand لا عاصم as no possessor of protection and من رحم as an appositive; al-Ṭabarī rejects these alternatives as unnecessary departures from ordinary Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي البصرة: {لا عاصم اليوم من أمر الله إلا من رحم} [هود: 43] على: لكن من رحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the common Arabic sense is clear without unusual grammar: only God can protect from His punishment, just as only God can deliver or provide food.
rows.anchor: إذ كنا نجد لذلك في معناه الذي هو معناه في المشهور من كلام العرب مخرجا صحيحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wave of water came between Noah and his son; the son drowned and became one of Noah's people destroyed by drowning.
rows.anchor: وحال بين نوح وابنه موج الماء، فغرق، فكان ممن أهلكه الله بالغرق من قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad must remain steadfast in the religion and call to it as God commanded, and those who returned with him must obey God after disbelief.
rows.anchor: طاعة الله، والعمل بما أمره به ربه من بعد كفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not transgress God's command by doing what He forbade; God sees and knows every act of obedience or disobedience, and nothing is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: طاعة الله، والعمل بما أمره به ربه من بعد كفره

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna interprets steadfastness as remaining upon the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: في قوله: " {فاستقم كما أمرت} [هود: 112] قال: استقم على القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd defines transgression as opposing God and committing disobedience.
rows.anchor: في قوله: " {ولا تطغوا} [هود: 112] قال: الطغيان: خلاف الله وركوب معصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to pray at the two ends of the day, morning and evening; all interpreters agree that the morning prayer is Fajr but differ over the evening prayer.
rows.anchor: إجماع جميعهم على أن التي عنيت من صلاة الغد: الفجر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the prayers as Fajr and the afternoon prayers, Zuhr and ʿAsr.
rows.anchor: قال: الفجر، وصلاتي العشي، يعني الظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb identifies the ends as Fajr, Zuhr, and ʿAsr.
rows.anchor: قال: فطرفا النهار: الفجر والظهر والعصر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the two end-of-day prayers are the morning prayer and Maghrib.
rows.anchor: يقول: صلاة الغداة وصلاة المغرب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan likewise identifies the prayers as Fajr and Maghrib.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، " {أقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} [هود: 114] قال. صلاة الغداة والمغرب

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the prayers are morning and Maghrib.
rows.anchor: في قوله: " {أقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} [هود: 114] الصبح، والمغرب

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the two prayers as Fajr and ʿAsr.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: " {أقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} [هود: 114] قال: صلاة الفجر والعصر

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, al-Hasan, and Qatada are reported as identifying the prayers at the two ends as Fajr and ʿAsr.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله " {أقم الصلاة طرفي النهار} [هود: 114] يعني صلاة العصر والصبح

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan is separately reported as naming the morning and ʿAsr prayers.
rows.anchor: قال: طرفي النهار: الغداة والعصر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the two ends are Zuhr and ʿAsr, while the night periods include Maghrib, ʿIsha, and Fajr.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: بل عنى بطرفي النهار: الظهر، والعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers Ibn ʿAbbas's pairing of Fajr and Maghrib: since everyone agrees one end is Fajr before sunrise, the other should be Maghrib after sunset; Zuhr and ʿAsr both fall in the day's latter half, not opposite ends.
rows.anchor: وأولى هذه الأقوال في ذلك عندي بالصواب قول من قال: هي صلاة المغرب كما ذكرنا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the Zuhr-and-ʿAsr proposal because Zuhr follows midday and is in the second half of the day, so it cannot be the first endpoint while ʿAsr is the other.
rows.anchor: فمحال أن تكون من طرف النهار الأول، وهي في طرفه الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī links the night phrase to the portion of night after which the ʿIsha prayer is performed.
rows.anchor: صلاة العشاء الآخرة إنما تصلى بعد مضي زلف من الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Medinan readers pronounce both letters with ḍamma, while some Meccan readers use a silent lam.
rows.anchor: وقرأه بعض أهل المدينة بضم الزاي واللام، كأنه وجهه إلى أنه واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the plural reading zulafan, with ḍamma on zay and fatḥa on lam, as the plural of zulfa; the ʿIsha prayer occurs after portions of night, matching the verse.
rows.anchor: وأعجب القراءات في ذلك إلي أن أقرأها: {وزلفا} [هود: 114] بضم الزاي وفتح اللام، على معنى جمع زلفة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, and Ibn Zayd are cited as taking the night periods to mean the ʿIsha prayer alone.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: " {وزلفا من الليل} [هود: 114] قال: الساعات من الليل صلاة العتمة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another group says the night periods refer to both Maghrib and ʿIsha; the report list continues in the next segment.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: الصلاة التي أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بإقامتها زلفا من الليل، صلاة المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the night periods are the two prayers, Maghrib and ʿIsha; the report attributes the same wording to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «هما زلفتا الليل المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and other interpreters are reported as identifying the night prayers as Maghrib and ʿIsha.
rows.anchor: عن سفيان عن منصور عن مجاهد " {وزلفا من الليل} [هود: 114] قال: المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan links prayer times to 17:78, naming dawn and ʿAsr at the day ends and Maghrib and ʿIsha as the night periods.
rows.anchor: قال: {أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل} [الإسراء: 78] قال: دلوكها: إذا زالت عن بطن السماء

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, al-Hasan, and al-Dahhak are among the authorities identifying the night periods as Maghrib and ʿIsha.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: " {وزلفا من الليل} [هود: 114] قال: المغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good deeds mean turning back to obedience and doing what pleases God; these acts remove the sins of disobedience and expiate transgressions.
rows.anchor: إن الإنابة إلى طاعة الله، والعمل بما يرضيه، يذهب آثام معصية الله ويكفر الذنوب

rows.speaker: كعب، محمد بن كعب القرظي، ابن عباس، مجاهد، الحسن، الضحاك
rows.claim: A number of early authorities identify the good deeds in this verse as the five obligatory prayers; Kaʿb compares them to water washing away dirt.
rows.anchor: إن الصلوات الخمس لهن الحسنات التي يذهبن السيئات كما يغسل الماء الدرن

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud identifies the good deeds as the five daily prayers.
rows.anchor: عن علقمة، عن عبد الله، " {إن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات} [هود: 114] قال: الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Salman says the five prayers wash sins away like water removes dirt, as the Prophet's teaching illustrated.
rows.anchor: إن الحسنات التي يمحو الله بهن السيئات كما يغسل الماء الدرن: الصلوات الخمس

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says the prayers serve as expiations for what occurs between them and cites this verse.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " جعلت الصلوات كفارات لما بينهن

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet tells Salman that a Muslim who performs ablution well and prays the five prayers has sins fall away like leaves shaken from a dry branch, then recites this verse.
rows.anchor: إن المسلم إذا توضأ فأحسن الوضوء، ثم صلى الصلوات الخمس، تحاتت خطاياه كما تحات هذا الورق
